# Workflow scripts — generated by Keel

These scripts are generated by Keel into `.claude/workflows/` alongside the project docs.
Two units of work, two script shapes:

- **Phase** (`phase-N-<slug>.js`) — a gated milestone. Creates one **phase branch** off `main`,
  fans out divisible work as parallel agents in separate `git worktree`s branched off it, merges
  each task back, runs **Verify** (the one place test suites run for evidence), runs doc-sync on
  the phase branch, then merges the phase branch — and only the phase branch — into `main` and
  flips deploy state to `[merged]`.
- **Change** (`chg-<slug>.js`) — hotfix-weight. One branch off `main`, one agent, one evidence
  record, doc-sync, merge. No phase block, no fan-out.

## Usage

```
claude --workflow .claude/workflows/phase-N-<slug>.js     # a phase
claude --workflow .claude/workflows/chg-<slug>.js         # a change
claude --workflow .claude/workflows/doc-sync.js           # standalone doc sync (before any manual merge)
```
Or paste the path into the Workflow tool inside a Claude Code session.
`/keel phase new <slug>` and `/keel change <slug>` generate these from the templates.

## Scripts in this project

| Script | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `doc-sync.js` | Mandatory pre-merge doc sync: status tables, exit-gate evidence, ADRs, deferred items, CHANGELOG; then byte-budget check + auto-archive |
| `phase-0-guardrails.js` | Phase 0: scaffold guardrails and CI |
| `phase-N-<slug>.js` | One script per IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN phase |
| `chg-<slug>.js` | One script per Change (generated by `/keel change`) |

## Stages and what each may claim

| Stage | Runs suites? | Writes | May write "prod-live"? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Setup | no | phase branch; reserved `docs/adr/ADR-NNN-<slug>.md` stubs (Proposed) | — |
| Build (per worktree) | yes, for itself | code + tests; fills its reserved ADR stub | no |
| Integrate | re-runs failing task tests only | merges; numbers `ADR-N-pending-*` stubs; renumbers colliding migrations | no |
| **Verify** | **yes — once, for evidence** | `.keel/evidence/phase-N.json` (+ raw reports, browser transcripts) | **no** |
| Doc Sync | **no — cites Verify** | exit-gate table, status table, ADR statuses, deferred, CHANGELOG `[on-branch]` | no |
| Merge | no | merge commit; flips `[on-branch]` → `[merged <sha>]` | no |
| Deploy (DEPLOYMENT.md procedure, outside these scripts) | post-deploy checklist | deploy log row; CHANGELOG `[deployed vNN]` → `[live-verified]` | **yes** |

Evidence levels: `code-read < unit < integration < local-browser < staging < prod-live`.
A gate whose wording demands a level Verify did not reach is `partial`, and the phase stays 🔄.

## Rules

- Never merge to trunk without a doc-sync commit and an evidence record.
- Never merge a task branch straight to trunk — task branches merge into the phase branch;
  only the phase branch (code + evidence + doc-sync commit) ever merges to trunk.
- Never share a worktree between agents — one task, one worktree.
- Doc-sync cites `.keel/evidence/*.json`; it never re-runs suites and never trusts a Build
  agent's own "it passes". Every ✅ carries a level and an artefact.
- Deploy state is written state-neutrally (`on \`branch\``) and flipped mechanically at merge —
  no "not yet merged" prose that needs a second commit.
- IDs never collide by construction: ADR numbers reserved in Setup; migrations timestamp-named;
  `ADR-N-pending-*` numbered at Integrate; CHG numbers allocated at Change setup.
- No ADR addenda. Build deviation = one ADR row · incident = RUNBOOK postmortem · deploy state =
  CHANGELOG / DEPLOYMENT deploy log · changed decision = new superseding ADR.
- Deferred items carry Owner (founder | engineering | legal) and a Revisit trigger — WHY and
  WHEN, not just WHAT. Negative results are recorded, not dropped.
- Every task agent opens with `/goal` — a completion condition that blocks it from ending its
  turn early; the `verify` skill and a `claude-in-chrome` pass for UI are part of the condition.
  The exit strategy when a goal isn't met is the project's Standing-rules policy; `/goal clear` is
  its deliberate escape hatch, never a way to fake completion.
- Byte budgets (`.keel/meta.json` → `budgets`) are enforced by doc-sync's Budget stage; a breach
  triggers one auto-archive pass (relocate, never delete) committed on its own. If nothing is
  archivable it reports `BUDGET_EXCEEDED` and stops — a human raises the budget or trims by hand.
